summary: FileVault recovery key mismatch after depot battery replacement; Secure Enclave serial reset blocks MDM profile re-enrollment
description:
Issue summary: After a depot battery replacement performed by the hardware team, we received reports that users were prompted for FileVault recovery keys and could not complete MDM profile re-enrollment. Impact: two engineers were unable to access their boot volumes without recovery keys; both devices are corporate owned and block daily work. Environment: depot repair bench in us-west; affected units are M1-based MacBook Pros imaged with corporate macOS baseline.

High level: During hardware replacement the Secure Enclave UID appears to have changed (manufacturer OTP written), resulting in a FileVault recovery key mismatch and the MDM (Intune/Company Portal) profile failing to validate signatures during re-enroll. This prevents SSO tokens and configuration profiles from applying and blocks Okta SSO for those devices.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Receive MacBook Pro (M1) to depot for battery replacement
2) Perform standard battery swap and reassembly following depot SOP 7.1
3) Boot device and run standard hardware post-checks; image not re-flashed (repair intended hardware-only),
4) Hand device back to user; user attempts to login — FileVault prompts for recovery key
5) Attempt to re-enroll into MDM via Company Portal; enrollment fails with profile signature / key mismatch errors
observed_behavior: FileVault prompts for a recovery key the original user cannot provide. Attempting to use the admin recovery key from asset record returns 'invalid recovery key'. Company Portal enrollment shows 'profile validation failed: secure enclave mismatch' and the MDM profile does not install. Device remains in a pre-login locked state or in a limited login state without corporate profiles.
logs: pmset -g log: no abnormal power events; hardware post-checks completed
system.log excerpt: 'SEED: SecureEnclaveUID changed from 0xA12F... to 0x5B8C... after battery swap'
company-portal: 'enrollment failed: profile signature invalid - SEP mismatch'
fdesetup: 'No matching recovery key found for this machine'
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Anna Martinez (Support): Ticket opened after user called desktop support. User reports immediate FileVault prompt after returning from depot repair.
2026-03-10 11:05 - Depot Tech (Jason L.): Confirmed battery replaced; we did not re-image per SOP. Noted firmware revisions applied by vendor tool during reassembly.

2026-03-11 08:30 - Ravi Patel (Endpoint Eng): Investigating SEP (Secure Enclave Processor) UID change. Requested serials and Secure Enclave logs from depot. Added to 'hardware-firmware-investigation' slack channel.
2026-03-11 13:46 - Depot Tech (Jason L.): Attached hardware exchange log and vendor battery tool output (firmware write steps), vendor reported writing OTP fuses during battery firmware update.

2026-03-12 10:02 - Ravi Patel (Endpoint Eng): Reproduced SEP UID flip on bench with sacrificial unit following vendor tool flow. Filing follow-on with supply chain and vendor; escalation to security for FileVault key handling guidance.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: vendor battery firmware tool writes or reinitializes a Secure Enclave identifier when performing a 'full reset' during battery firmware update. SEP UID change invalidates locally bound FileVault keys and MDM profile signatures.
Bench repro: used identical model and vendor tool; observed SEP UID increment after tool step 'SEPFuse: burn = 1'. FileVault keys tied to SEP UID — keyslot invalid when UID changes.

MDM enrollment failure maps to internal error code SEP_UID_MISMATCH (0x14) in our profile validation library. Profile signatures are bound to device SEP UID metadata for anti-tamper — mismatch results in explicit rejection.

Confirmed both affected users had not been re-imaged. Standard depot SOP avoids re-image for battery swaps; this SOP may be insufficient for M1-era devices when vendor firmware utilities touch SEP fuses.
Related risk: if vendor tooling is modifying SEP data during common battery swap workflow, repair bench could be inadvertently orphaning recovery keys across a population.
mitigation_steps: 1) For affected devices: escalate to security and follow FileVault key recovery runbook to decrypt volume in controlled environment and rekey to new SEP UID under management direction.

2) Temporarily change depot SOP: require re-image (or SEP-safe firmware path) for any battery replacement that triggers vendor firmware writes. Immediately stop using vendor tool step 'SEPFuse: burn' until vendor confirms behavior.
3) Notify asset owners and desktop support to hold devices from return to users pending resolution for devices repaired since 2026-03-01.
4) Collect full list of depot repairs in window and identify potentially affected serials for targeted outreach.
next_steps: Coordinate with Supply Chain and vendor (battery vendor) to determine why their tool writes to SEPFuse and whether there is a 'no-op' firmware path that preserves SEP UID.
Work with Security to authorize controlled rekey/recovery for impacted volumes and issue temporary policy for depot handling of T2/SE devices.
Update depot SOP and push training to depot technicians; add a precheck step to detect SEP-write operations in vendor tool output.
Consider automation: on device intake, capture SEP UID and store in asset DB; verify post-repair SEP UID matches pre-repair before returning to user.
resolution_notes: (pending) Vendor is investigating an option to skip writing SEPFuse during battery firmware update. Until vendor confirms, depot team will re-image devices post-battery-repair as a temporary control.
(pending) Security approved a supervised rekey and re-enrollment procedure for affected volumes; formal steps to be added to confluence runbook after vendor sign-off.

(workaround) For critical users we performed supervised decryption using recovery escrow and rekeyed FileVault after SEP reinitialization; device re-enrolled into MDM and returned to user on 2026-03-12.
